chat.footer: private messages and live rooms on nostr relays · sealed on your device
chat.title: Messages
chat.rooms.title: Live rooms
chat.rooms.text: Talk with anyone who has the link: no account needed, nothing stored anywhere, gone when the room empties.
chat.rooms.placeholder: Paste a room link or code
chat.rooms.invalid: That is not a room link or code.
chat.empty: No conversations yet. Message a friend, or start a room.
chat.noFriends: Messages go to friends. Add some in the site settings.
chat.blocked: You blocked this person. Their messages are hidden.
chat.blockedDone: Blocked. Their messages are gone from every device.
chat.forgetText: It disappears from this device only. The other person keeps their copy, and your other devices keep theirs.
chat.room.title: Room
chat.room.empty: Nothing has been said since you came in. Nothing from before is kept anywhere.
chat.room.hint: Everything in the room is sealed with a key that lives only in its link. Relays pass messages on and keep nothing.
chat.settings.nickHint: Suggested when you enter a room; you can change it each time.
chat.how.1: Live rooms are ephemeral nostr events sealed with a key that lives only in the room’s link: relays pass them to whoever is in the room and store nothing, so a room has no history and leaves nothing behind.
chat.groups.title: Groups
chat.groups.empty: No groups yet. Make one, open a link someone sent you, or start a live room.
chat.groups.joinPlaceholder: Paste a group or room link
chat.group.title: Group
chat.group.name: Name of the group
chat.group.newHint: A group stays until you close it. Members are people you or they let in; the invite link opens no door by itself.
chat.group.knockText: You have a link to “{name}”. Ask to be let in; the host sees your name and your key.
chat.group.waiting: Waiting for the host of “{name}” to let you in.
chat.group.waitingHint: The host’s device answers when it is online. You can close this; the request stays with your account.
chat.group.hint: Everything in a group is sealed with keys only its members hold; relays see one anonymous author.
chat.group.empty: Nothing has been said here yet.
chat.group.linkReset: New invite link. Links given out before no longer open the door.
chat.group.openOn: Anyone with the link may join
chat.group.invited: Invited {n}. They are in as soon as their device picks it up.
chat.group.leaveText: The group disappears from your devices. The others get a new key, so what they say after this stays theirs.
chat.group.closeText: It disappears from every member’s devices. Relays keep only sealed events nobody will open.
chat.group.removeText: Their devices drop the group, and everyone else gets a new key: what is said from now on stays among you.
chat.invites.title: Invitations
chat.invites.room: {name} invites you to a live room
chat.groups.hint: Invite friends from inside a group or a room: they get it sealed, in the chat, and say yes or no here. A link is for people who are not friends yet; it lets them knock, nothing more. A live room keeps nothing and is gone when it empties.
chat.deleteText: It goes from the conversation on every device that runs this app, yours and theirs. Someone may have read or kept it already, and another app may still show it.
chat.replyMissing: A message that is not on this device
chat.timer.title: Disappearing messages
chat.timer.text: New messages disappear after the time you choose, for everyone in the conversation.
chat.timer.hint: They go from every device running this app and from relays that keep to expiry dates (NIP-40). Anyone could still have kept a copy, with a screenshot or another app.
chat.search.title: Search
chat.search.hint: Searches the conversations and groups on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere.
chat.how.2: Replies, reactions, edits, pins and deletions are sealed events of their own, sent like the messages and applied on every device. A deletion or a timer takes a message off every device running this app and off relays that keep to expiry dates (NIP-40); it cannot reach a copy someone already kept.
call.bar: In a call with {name}: back to it
call.failed: No direct connection to {name}. Between some networks (two phones on mobile data, for one) a call needs a TURN server, which this hub does not name.
call.busy: You are in a call already.
chat.how.3: Calls go straight between the browsers (WebRTC, encrypted end to end by DTLS-SRTP). Ringing is a sealed message like any other; the browsers find each other through sealed events on the hub’s relays that the relays do not keep. A group call connects everyone with everyone, so it suits a few people. Where no direct path exists, only a TURN server the hub names gets a call through; it passes the encrypted media on and cannot hear them.
